points.description: States that a pointer is a variable that holds/stores/contains the memory address of another variable (or of a memory location/object).
points.partial_credit: Half or more of the marks if only vague or partial: e.g. says it 'points to' or 'refers to' another variable, or says it stores an address without saying it is a variable, or has a minor error.

points.description: Makes clear that the address it holds belongs to another variable (the pointer refers to something else in memory, not to its own value).

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable, in any wording (e.g. 'it holds where another variable is stored'). Give part marks for vague answers such as 'it points to another variable' or 'it stores an address' without the other half. Give no marks for answers that only describe pointer syntax or uses (e.g. dynamic memory) without saying it holds an address, or that say it holds a value.
